newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran criticises Turkish remarks on northern Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Iran criticises Turkish remarks on northern Iraq.

text.p: Iran on Wednesday expressed regret over remarks by Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller that Tehran might be meddling in inter-Kurdish fighting in northern Iraq, the Iranian news agency IRNA said.

It said an Iranian foreign ministry source regretted the remarks and reiterated Iran's denial that it backed the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) in its drive against the Baghdad-backed Kurdistan Democratic Party.

"Iran has always been in the belief that backing any group in northern Iraq would only heighten tension there and that regional countries...should help ease tension in the region," IRNA quoted the source as saying.
Ciller said on Tuesday: "We have received certain information along the lines of Iranians inside (PUK leader Jalal) Talabani's forces."
Iran on Tuesday offered to mediate between the warring Kurdish factions in northern Iraq.
Ankara last month criticised Tehran for failing to prevent infiltrations of separatist Kurds into Turkey from Iran.
Iran rejected the accusations, complaining that outlawed Iranian opposition groups were operating from Turkey.
